title: Intrinsic finite-dualizing restriction composition
statement: For n ≤ m ≤ r and every object K of the pro-etale derived category at level n, the inverse intrinsic finite-dualizing restriction comparison for n ≤ r, followed by the inverse normalized restriction compositor, equals the pro-etale derived scalar compositor inverse, followed by the inverse intrinsic comparison for m ≤ r and the normalized restriction image of the inverse intrinsic comparison for n ≤ m.

source.place: Final sentence: transport by the finite dualizing comparison, with identity and successive-coefficient normalization

proof.text: The section-normalized intrinsic comparison is uniquely characterized on scalar-unit sections. Quotient maps compose on representatives, so the direct and successive comparisons have the same normalization. Uniqueness transports this equality through exact derived localization; pasting with the canonical derived scalar and normalized restriction compositors gives the stated component identity.

theorem finiteDualizingIntrinsicRestriction_comp
    {r m n : ℕ} (hrm : m ≤ r) (hmn : n ≤ m)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (ProEt.topology X)
      (ModuleCat (finiteDualizingCoeff l E n)))) :
    (finiteDualizingIntrinsicRestriction l E X (hmn.trans hrm)).inv.app K ≫
        (normalizedDVRResComp l E X hrm hmn).inv.app
          ((sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence X
            (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1))).functor.obj K) =
      (sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence X
          (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (r + 1))).functor.map
        ((Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalarsCompIso (ProEt.topology X)
          (finiteDualizingQuotient_comp l E hrm hmn)).inv.app K) ≫
        (finiteDualizingIntrinsicRestriction l E X hrm).inv.app
          ((Sheaf.derivedRestrictScalars (ProEt.topology X)
            (finiteDualizingQuotient l E hmn)).obj K) ≫
        (normalizedDVRRes l E X hrm).map
          ((finiteDualizingIntrinsicRestriction l E X hmn).inv.app K)
